headline: Tooling is 12 primitives; only 1 has its cost measured
brief: The team asked whether to adopt a million community 'skills'. A skill is one of twelve kinds of agent tooling, and each kind is judged by different tests. We built the map: every kind, the real tests that exist for it, and whether anyone checks what it COSTS to plug in. Almost nobody does — and cost is exactly what 'bloated' means.

headline: Public for real this time — verified from outside, not inside
brief: Yesterday's attempt looked clean from my own machine and still leaked, because rewriting history does not remove old copies from GitHub's servers. So instead of editing the old repo, I made a brand new one and copied only the clean work into it. Then I checked from the outside, as a stranger would, and the old copies genuinely do not exist there.
